o.text: Borrowed from Russian бана́н (banán), from French banane, from Portuguese banana or Spanish banana. Ultimately from Wolof banaana.
Probably from Old Anatolian Turkish [script needed] (yorı-, “to walk”). Alternatively, a regular derivation from yor- (“to tire”) + -ul, ultimately from Proto-Common Turkic *yor-.
Borrowed from Classical Persian سِنْدَان (sindān). For the initial voicing of /s/, see Azerbaijani zəngin.
From Proto-Turkic *čïgïr (“foot path, narrow track”). Cognate with Tatar and Turkish çığır.
From gələcəkçi (“futurist; futuristic”) + -lik (“-ness”). Compare Turkish gelecekçilik.
Borrowed from Turkish duygulanmak. Equivalent to duyğu + -lan.
